sources.entry: Qingo - Cache cleaner that recognizes 60+ video, design and AI tools (CapCut, DaVinci Resolve, Adobe apps, Cursor, Claude Code and more), clears only caches that rebuild automatically, and moves them to the Trash with undo, leaving projects and conversations untouched (Chinese UI). [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/chenmozhe008/qingo) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][N

summary.one_liner: Qingo (小清) is a native SwiftUI macOS cleanup app, with a Chinese UI, that removes rebuildable caches from video, design, AI and developer tools while leaving projects, conversations and models alone.
summary.what_it_does: Qingo scans a Mac for caches created by video editing, design, AI assistant, AI coding and local model tools, including CapCut/剪映, DaVinci Resolve, Adobe apps, Cursor, Claude Code and Ollama. The quick scan lists only caches it can determine will rebuild automatically, selected by default, and moves them to the Trash. Cleanup can be undone within 15 seconds from the result bar, or restored from the Trash. It also has a developer build cache view for project folders (default ~/Coding), a large-file scan (full scan of the user directory), and an app uninstaller that moves an app's support files, caches and preferences to the Trash. The app notifies when free space drops below 10 GB and can show a report of space changes between scans. It checks GitHub for updates at most once a day, which can be turned off, and the README says it uploads no data. WeChat and WeCom folders are reported with their paths but never deleted.
use_cases: clear rebuildable caches from video editors like CapCut or DaVinci Resolve
free disk space taken by AI coding tools and local models
clean developer package caches for npm, pip and uv
find and remove build caches in project folders
uninstall a Mac app along with its leftover support files
review large files and installers before deleting them
how_to_run: Download Qingo-.zip from Releases, unzip it, and drag 小清 into the Applications folder
On first launch, allow the unsigned app in System Settings > Privacy & Security, or run: xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/小清.app
Optional: enable 小清 under Full Disk Access to scan WeChat and more caches
git clone the repository and cd into qingo
notable: Tool-by-tool recognition: it separates rebuildable caches from projects, chats and models in each app's folders
Undo window of 15 seconds and Trash-only deletion, with no permanent delete
Cleanup rules are all in the source code (Sources/Qingo/CreativeApps.swift) for review
Developer build cache view that scans code folders in the background and is kept separate from the one-click cleanup
Free-space alerts and a space-change report that lists what grew since the last quick scan
caveats: Requires macOS 14 Sonoma or later and Apple silicon (M1 or newer)
Not notarized by Apple, so first launch needs a manual approval step, and Full Disk Access must be re-enabled after each update
The UI is in Chinese; the README is mainly in Chinese with an English version linked
Without Full Disk Access, protected folders such as WeChat are not read and not counted
